# Julia CUDA UInt32 reference (#560)

`curand_julia.txt` is generated by `gen_curand_julia.jl` using Julia 1.13.1,
CUDA.jl 6.4.2 and the GPU reference at
`47452f9061ec3de049d891a7aa7fd9cfeac228a4`. The generator uses actual
`CUDA.seed!` and `CUDA.rand(UInt32, n)` calls, including consecutive odd-sized
draws, zero-sized draws, draws spanning 4096 library states, 64-bit seeds and
reseed. Expected values are not generated by Rust.

The Julia process loaded its artifact CUDA 13.4 runtime and **cuRAND 10.4.4**;
setting `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` did not replace Julia's artifact library. Rust tests
were run against cuRAND **10.3.9.90** from the CUDA 12.8 library directory. All
33,476 words agree exactly. This verifies these two installed versions; it is
not a promise about all future default cuRAND orderings.

The cuRAND library's default XORWOW sequence interleaves generator states.
Giving each walker a standalone `curand_init(seed, ...)` state does not reproduce
this tape. See NVIDIA's [host API ordering documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/curand/host-api-overview.html#order).
Rust retains one library generator per ensemble and binds it to the sampling
stream, so it needs neither a host tape nor a barrier between RNG and sampling.

Generation hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (sm_86), driver 580.178.04,
`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1`. Reproduction command is in the script header.
